description: The boat code was written into the register after the rescue, so it is only filled in for people who were picked up: about 98% of passengers with a code survived, against 6% of those without one. That is information from after the outcome, so a model trained on it cheats. groupby(df.boat.notna())[‘survived’].mean() exposes it at once. This is the famous leak in the real Titanic dataset, whose ‘boat’ and ‘body’ columns give the answer away; this register is synthetic and the Carrow Belle is fictional.
hints: Ask of every column: could the clerk have known this on the day she sailed? Then compare each column against the survival rate.
Try grouping the survival rate by whether each column is filled in or blank. One text column splits survivors from the lost almost perfectly.
The boat code only exists for people who got into a lifeboat, and it was written down after the rescue. Passengers with a code survived about 98% of the time.
